title: Opening Night 🎉
description:
Doors open at 4.30pm, and content kicks off at Centre Stage at 6pm. You'll need to be registered and have collected your wristband and lanyard to enter.

Speakers include Tao Zhang, Co-founder, Manus AI; Matthew Prince, Co-founder & CEO, Cloudflare; Anton Osika, Co-founder & CEO, Lovable; Richard Socher, Co-founder & CEO, Recursive; Deli Zhao, Founder & President, Xpeng Aridge UBTech U1 Pro - Ultra-realistic Humanoid Robot; UBTech Walker C1; Yuli Zhao, CSO, Galbot; Galbot G1 - Embodied Large-Model Robot; William Shi, President, Europe & Americas, AGIBOT A3; AGIBOT X2 Ultra; and Paddy Cosgrave, CEO of Web Summit.

Join us for an unforgettable evening filled with great speakers, networking, and more.

Don't leave early! 
After the opening ceremony, follow the path through the Food and Wine Summit straight into Night Summit in Pavilion 5. Get ready to make spontaneous connections through speed networking, karaoke sessions, meet & greets activities and more.

We can’t wait to see you there!

Please note: This event has limited capacity.

title: The age of agents
description: Forget AGI and chatbots; we’ve officially entered the age of agents. Far beyond standard LLMs, AI agents are embedding into everyday apps to independently solve real-life problems and handle complex tasks. Join Manus AI Co-founder and CPO Tao Zhang - who pioneered agents - to explore why the shift to autonomous agents matters more than the latest foundation model, how it will change daily life for billions, and why the race to control the agent interface is the battle to become tech's next dominant giant.

title: The future of AI
description: From Anthropic’s historic IPO filing to sharp swings across global tech stocks, the AI industry has reached a defining inflection point. As markets demand genuine enterprise adoption and real-world value over speculative hype, how do we build what comes next? Bringing together key architects of the next era, this panel tackles what AI looks like when the dust settles.

title: Welcome to tomorrow
description: Cars that take to the sky. Embodied AI that walks among us. Robots serving our coffee. The future isn't approaching; it's already operating - in China that is. Join us for an exclusive, first-of-its-kind showcase bringing China’s most advanced next-generation robotics and aerial mobility to Europe. Step beyond the horizon and witness the technology shaping tomorrow, before it reaches the rest of the world!

description: For decades, Europe has depended on the US not only for its security, but also for much of its technological and financial infrastructure. As the transatlantic relationship continues to fracture, Europe faces a question much bigger than how to spend more on defence. Can it reduce its dependence on American technology, capital and financial infrastructure while building the industrial capacity to defend itself? And can it do so without sacrificing prosperity and the welfare state?

title: Are job interviews real anymore?
description: Behind viral social clips of applicants using AI to cheat virtual interviews lies a threat to corporate security: synthetic candidates infiltrating core enterprise systems. As generative video, real-time voice cloning and AI-inflated profiles proliferate, traditional candidate verification is failing. In this session we examine the mechanics of the fake candidate epidemic. In this session we explore how to shut down synthetic fraud before it reaches the payroll.

title: In the age of AI, trust is still human

title: Everything will be simulated

title: Rethinking venture capital
description: As market cycles tighten and exits take longer, standard financial backing isn't enough to help startups succeed. Modern venture capital requires a complete support structure to lower risk and speed up growth. This session focuses on what it takes to turn complex ideas into durable, market-ready companies.

title: Machine-ready brands: A playbook for the Intelligence Age
description: Customers are getting used to agents doing the browsing, deciding, even the buying on their behalf. Once someone's used to that, a static ad or a fixed website starts to feel broken. They expect brands to meet them with the same fluency: responsive, individualized, always-on. This talk explores what it takes to define a brand for both humans and machines, and build the systems that keep it consistent, current, and everywhere your customers now expect to find it.

title: The AI paradox: Smarter models, disappointing results
description: AI models are becoming more powerful at a breathtaking pace. So why aren't businesses seeing the transformation they were promised? Glean CEO Arvind Jain challenges the industry's obsession with model intelligence alone, examines what AI companies are getting wrong about context, and explores what it will actually take to turn AI's extraordinary capabilities into real-world impact.

title: Your AI agent just got a passport
description: AI agents are moving from experiments to real-world use. But success in one market doesn't guarantee success elsewhere. Language, culture and local expectations all shape how people interact with AI. RWS CEO Benjamin Faes explores what businesses need to consider when building AI for a complex, multilingual world.

title: The battery is the new barrel
description: From raw lithium extraction to fast-charging grid deployment, batteries are reshaping modern energy security. This session examines how critical minerals, battery storage, and EV infrastructure unite to build flexible, resilient, and independent energy systems.

title: Live Podcast: The Big Technology Podcast with Atlassian
description: If Software Was Dead, Why Are We Sitting Here? AI agents were supposed to destroy software companies, But so far, that prediction looks premature or wrong. Atlassian co-founder Mike Cannon-Brookes joins Big Technology’s Alex Kantrowitz to examine why SaaS has held up and what happens as agents start operating software on our behalf. In this talk, they’ll explore whether organisational context (not necessarily model intelligence) is becoming the key advantage in enterprise AI, whether the traditional software interface survives, and where, if at all, the “Saaspocalypse” worries had merit.

title: From 'For You' to 'For Me': The new path from discovery to action
description: On TikTok, people watch it, love it, want it – and increasingly, those moments happen almost all at once. What starts as entertainment can spark curiosity, inspire a search, shape a decision and drive action, reshaping the traditional path from awareness to purchase. This talk explores how this new era of discovery is changing marketing, from the growing influence of creators and communities to the role of AI in creativity, and how brands can turn cultural relevance into real business growth.

title: The future has a following
description: From TikTok to the Times, traditional media is turning to creators to rebuild relationships with audiences who have turned away. In a bid to stay relevant, legacy outlets are enlisting creator clout to stay in the conversation. But does this represent a genuine, long-term partnership – or is it merely a temporary fix while traditional media tries to catch up.

description: Mental health care is undergoing a fundamental transformation, driven by advances in behavioural psychology, digital therapeutics, and generative AI. In this talk, MindFriend founder Sheikha Maytha Bint Maktoum and ambassador Zahara Marley Jolie explore how AI can break down barriers to women’s mental health worldwide, while confronting critical questions of safety, trust, and responsible innovation.

title: The women unmasking digital crime scenes
description: The internet isn’t safe or regulated – and now, it has also become a crime scene. A dangerous digital underworld is emerging as hidden groups on Telegram and public porn websites host international rape networks. As these networks expand globally, more and more women are being harmed. This panel brings together the journalists who exposed these covert networks hiding in plain sight.

title: Fusion's fork in the road

Each offers unique scientific advantages, engineering risks, and economic realities. With billions invested and global energy security on the line, which approach will cross the finish line first, and which could be left behind?

title: Everything you need to know about M&A in 2026
description: Navigating tech M&A in 2026 requires a playbook built for scale, integration, and sustainable value creation. This session breaks down the realities of 2026 dealmaking, from executing multi-market consolidation strategies to evaluating AI-driven targets. Gain practical insights from an experienced global finance leader on how to identify acquisition targets, manage regulatory hurdles, and extract true post-merger value in today’s evolving market.

title: Bet on the foundation, not the framework
description: Most conversations about AI independence focus on the model: who trains it, who owns the weights, and where inference runs. Samar Abbas, co-founder and CEO of Temporal, will argue that's the wrong place to look. The layer that matters is underneath: the execution infrastructure that decides whether a company can actually change course later. Frameworks and agent harnesses are cycling through versions faster than almost anything else in tech. Whatever framework looks essential this year will likely be replaced next year. Samar's argument: building capable AI agents means building on an open foundation that outlasts the model, framework, or harness sitting on top of it, and that no single vendor can take away. Drawing on Temporal's work running durable execution under some of today's most demanding AI workloads, he'll make the case that the real question isn't which model you pick, but whether your infrastructure survives whatever comes next.

title: Can you trust what you see anymore?
description: AI has made it easier than ever to create content – text, video, and audio. But much of what it creates has very little relationship with reality. In a world flooded with slop, how can we trust what we watch, read, and hear?

title: Sensing the future: Using AI to unlock the next generation of molecular science.
description: What happens when AI moves beyond digital interfaces to interact with the physical and chemical world? From digitising scent and mapping molecular behaviour to creating sustainable food systems, AI is turning raw data into real-world sensory intelligence. This session demonstrates how AI-driven science is opening up multibillion-dollar opportunities across health, consumer products and global food infrastructure.

title: The agentic internet: Who controls the web?

As more activity happens without a human click, the web is facing new questions about control, attribution, and value. Cloudflare co-founder and CEO Matthew Prince explains why the internet is at a turning point - what this shift means for companies of every size and what it will take to keep the web open in the agentic era.

title: Regulation is killing European fintech

It protects consumers, but it also protects incumbents, raises the cost of experimentation and arguably explains a big chunk of why Europe keeps falling behind the U.S. and Asia in producing category-defining companies. In this conversation we're exploring how regulation in Europe is death by a thousand rules.

title: What makes a startup fundable in 2026?

title: Leading accessibility in the AI era: New challenges, new opportunities

In this fireside chat, Juan Pablo will discuss what changes when a founder gets the opportunity to build at scale for a second time. What did he learn from Rappi about international expansion, operating through hypergrowth and building in emerging markets? What did he deliberately do differently at Yuno? And how does starting again with the benefit of experience change decisions around product, capital, hiring and growth?

title: The intelligence behind AI commerce

Join Michael Komasinski as he examines the infrastructure that determines which products get suggested, which brands get surfaced, and which retailers capture attention at the moment of decision. title: Spotting durable tech in an era of bubble valuations

title: Leading the newsroom away from burnout

title: The great wealth divide: “Own assets or be left behind?"

That divide has become even more pronounced amid the AI revolution, with a further widening gap between those who own assets and those who do not. In this talk, Adam Kobeissi explores this and the impact of AI on markets and the economy.

description: As major game studios open their IP to community creators, building in-game content has become a viable career path. These creators, who build mods, apps, and tools for popular video games, are fuelling one of gaming's fastest-growing economies. title: The quantum leap for AI
description: What happens when quantum computing meets AI? Discover how these powerful technologies could push beyond today’s computational limits, unlock new approaches to discovery and problem-solving, and reshape what’s possible. We’ll explore what’s driving the race toward this new computing paradigm, where today’s AI may hit a wall, and how quantum technologies could open the door to breakthroughs we can only begin to imagine.

description: Sport generated $521 billion globally in 2024, but still lags other sectors in technology adoption. NXTPLAY is betting that the next big opportunity lies in connecting the pieces: football clubs, media, technology and consumer brands in an ecosystem where each asset strengthens the next, and athletes become owners and operators rather than simply the faces of a campaign. Thibaut Courtois and Gonzalo Vila discuss building the layer missing from modern sport.

title: AI filmmaking and the crisis of mediocrity
description: Generative AI hasn't ruined cinema, but low-effort digital content threatens to drown it. Drawing on over a decade in commercial filmmaking and photography, Kavan the Kid approaches synthetic cinema with technical precision and artistic discipline that has drawn audiences to his "Chronicles of Bone" YouTube series in their millions. Discover how generative tools empower independent storytellers to build original IP, bypass traditional studio gatekeeping, and turn fan-driven worlds into highly profitable media enterprises.

title: Building a new model for creators and journalism
description: Creators are no longer just another distribution channel for traditional media. They are becoming partners in how journalism reaches and engages new audiences. Sara Goo, President of The Washington Post’s Creator Network, explores what it takes to build meaningful partnerships between independent creators and an established newsroom. She’ll unpack how the Post is developing a model that gives creators space to retain their distinctive voices while drawing on the credibility and journalistic expertise of the newsroom — and how those partnerships can unlock new approaches to storytelling, audience engagement and revenue. What does a successful creator–newsroom partnership look like, and could this model reshape how journalism reaches the next generation of news consumers?

In his latest book, Pulitzer Prize-winning author Benjamin Moser explores the long and often overlooked history of Jewish opposition to Zionism. Through the lives and ideas of 12 Jewish thinkers, writers and activists, he challenges the assumption that Zionism has always been synonymous with Jewish identity. In this conversation, Moser discusses the historical roots of Jewish anti-Zionism, how it has evolved, and what its history can tell us about the politics of Israel, Palestine and Jewish identity today.

But agents can only do this if they have the right security, governance, and controls. Robots are beginning to learn, adapt and perform new tasks in the real world without being programmed for every situation. Abhinav Gupta, Co-Founder and President of Skild AI, explores the rise of Physical AI, why one general-purpose brain could power many different robots, and what it will take to bring intelligent machines into our factories, workplaces and everyday lives.

title: Disrupting the playbook: How unlikely alliances unlock growth
description: Companies often get trapped by their own industry’s rules and miss out on gamechanging deals. This session breaks down how cross-industry collaborations can spark the next wave of growth and spot new opportunities.

title: Scaling faster with AI employees
description: AI is moving out of standalone apps and into the places where teams already work. AI employees now sit in Slack and Microsoft Teams alongside human colleagues, taking on multi-step work with full organisational context. Join viktor.com co-founder Fryderyk Wiatrowski as he shares insights from companies deploying their first AI employees: which tasks get handed off, where humans retain control of high-stakes decisions and what teams look like when every employee has an AI colleague in their corner.

title: Women leading marketing in the age of AI Agents
description:
What does it mean to lead marketing when AI agents become part of the team? This panel explores how women in marketing leadership can turn new technology into meaningful customer experiences and business results. From CRM and personalisation to brand strategy, the conversation will look at where agents can add value, where human judgement remains essential, and how leaders can prepare their teams for new ways of working while protecting customer trust.

This session is limited to 100 people, with spots available on a first-come, first-served basis.

title: Bits vs atoms: Who wins the AI value capture race?
description: As AI moves from novelty to necessity, a high-stakes question emerges: Will the biggest financial returns come from digital software or the physical world? Join this session as leading investors debate where the true value of AI will be built. From intelligent software agents transforming office work to physical AI powering factories and robots, we break down where smart money is betting, where the strongest business moats lie, and what it takes to build a multi-billion-dollar AI company today.

title: Legacy media’s next move
description: Can traditional media leaders move fast enough to stay relevant in a rapidly changing landscape and what does it take to lead organisations through rapid disruption? Media leaders explore the future of established media, from embracing innovation and digital transformation to building trust, protecting editorial independence and winning the attention of a new generation of audiences.

title: The creative war: Is AI the weapon?
description: Is AI an enemy to be feared or is it a new soldier in the creative war? Like any powerful tool, AI demands judgement. When machines flood the market with cheap imitation, the danger isn’t that technology is too smart, it’s that our standards have become too low. The result: a race to the bottom. Join Brian Collins as he cuts through industry hype to reframe how we can build, design and create alongside AI, proving that technology should serve human vision, not replace it.

title: AI: doom or boom?
description: From absolute deregulation to heavy precautionary mandates, AI policy has become deeply polarised. Are we being forced to choose between Wild West growth and regulatory gridlock? Join us for a candid discussion on finding a pragmatic middle path, one that safeguards society without choking innovation or concentrating power in the hands of a few tech giants.

title: The death of feature moat
description: If your competitive advantage is a thin UI wrapper on someone else's foundation model, you don't have a moat, you have a countdown timer. When any rival can clone your entire product roadmap over a weekend, features stop being differentiators. Join Granola's Sam Stephenson and Ragged Edge's Max Ottignon as they expose the engineering-first delusion, revealing why radical brand identity, opinionated craft, and taste are the only defensible moats that survive in the AI era.

title: The token trap: Precision over power
description: As enterprises move from AI pilots to AI agents, per-token pricing turns every task into a metered cost, making ROI hard to predict and scale hard to justify. The answer is not bigger models. This keynote explores why precision and context deliver better results than raw model size, and how GaiaB, Austriacard's sovereign generative AI, runs agentic AI on-premises at zero token cost, keeping data, IP and costs under the enterprise's control.

title: Whose AI is it anyway? (Live field experiment)
description: As AI becomes a gateway to information and truth, the values embedded within LLMs become a political issue. Do AI systems developed in the US, China and Europe answer the same questions differently, and if so what are the implications? This live field experiment explores this issue. Our panel will put questions to a range of LLMs, examine the resulting responses and assess how politics, regulation and culture have shaped these different responses.

title: After Hours: Conspiracy theories - Is the truth out there?
description: History is full of genuine conspiracies. Powerful elites conspiring to advance their own self interest. Our expert "After Hours" panel discusses why conspiracy theories are so seductive, how real conspiracies have actually worked in practice, and whether our obsession with hidden plots tell us more about ourselves than about the world, or vice versa.

title: The future of enterprise software has no middleman
description: The engineering queue used to gatekeep what got built. Now, the person closest to the problem can build the solution for it: employees inside nearly two-thirds of the Fortune 500 already do. When software stops being a specialist job, that changes how companies build, staff, and ship. Anton Osika, Lovable's co-founder and CEO, will talk about what this transformation already looks like inside real companies, and what it takes to keep software secure when anyone can ship it.

title: Beyond the autonomous legal department

title: Who wins in the age of agentic AI?
description: As agentic AI transforms how we work, a critical question is emerging: where will the greatest value be created? Will it be the platforms powering the AI revolution, or the startups building the next generation of products and services? Bringing together Tencent's perspective as a global technology investor and Granola's experience building an AI-native product, this conversation explores where the biggest opportunities lie, what gives AI startups a competitive edge, and what it takes to build the next generation of global technology leaders.

title: Why your AI agents don’t understand your business – and how to fix it
description: Throwing an autonomous agent at a folder of unstructured PDFs and vector embeddings is a recipe for catastrophic hallucination. Agents fail not because foundation models lack intelligence; they fail for lack of context: the ontology, institutional memory, and semantics that actually define your business. Join Neo4j’s Philip Rathle to learn how to create a living knowledge graph as the “business twin” of your organization, giving agents the context to reason through real-world workflows without human babysitting, and solving for accuracy and explainability, and keeping token in check.

title: The model was never the product
description: In 2022, Jasper was one of the biggest names in AI. Six weeks after it became a unicorn, ChatGPT made its core offering free overnight. Very few companies survive that. Jasper did, first as a platform, and then as an applied AI company that embeds engineers and marketers inside enterprise teams. Join Jasper CEO Timothy Young will talk about what enterprise AI transformation really takes and why selling software alone is no longer enough.

title: The end of genius
description: The recent advances in generative AI are profoundly changing how we create text and images. But culturally, our beliefs about how creativity happens are stuck in the 18th century, shaped by a handful of German Romantic thinkers. The myth of the lone genius collides with systems that suggest that everything is simply a matter of computation. This talk explores whether AI will ultimately democratize creativity, or whether it spells the very end of the idea that made it culturally so important in the first place.

title: The case for play
description: What if play is not the opposite of serious work, but one of our most powerful tools for solving serious problems? IDEO Partner and Managing Director Michelle Lee explores how play can unlock creativity, challenge assumptions and help people navigate complexity, from product design and workplace culture to the age of AI.

title: The new curriculum. How education is evolving in the age of AI
description: As AI reshapes professional skills and labour market demands, traditional higher education faces a growing need to adapt. Bringing together academic leaders from Instituto Superior Técnico, and Ânima Educação, this session explores the transformation of post-secondary education. Discover how institutions are moving beyond legacy syllabi to embrace experiential global learning, real-time AI tools and cross-border project ecosystems.

title: The ultimate competitive edge: How companies can thrive through disruption
description: In a world where AI, technology, markets and geopolitics can shift faster than corporate strategies, the ability to change is becoming a competitive capability in its own right. This session explores what it takes to build organisations that can continuously adapt, moving faster from insight to decision, from decision to execution and from transformation to lasting performance.

title: How AI turns visual understanding into real work
description: What happens when AI that sees the physical world connects directly to AI that acts on it? This session explores how spatial intelligence on the factory floor translates into automated enterprise execution.

title: The intelligence paradox: Why greater AI power makes human expertise more valuable
description: Accumulating the most AI tools is not the race that will set companies apart. Instead, the organisations pulling ahead are those tackling the unglamorous groundwork everyone else is skipping. Successful firms select tools directly, properly train their workforce and keep human expertise at the centre of every critical judgment call. Aaron Gibson, founder and CEO of Hurree, will expose where most rollouts go wrong and reveal what the handful of companies getting this right do differently.

title: China’s quantum answer to global challenges
description: How can quantum computing help address challenges that matter to us all? China is pairing quantum with classical supercomputers to solve critical issues, including climate change, drug discovery and energy forecasting. Blending computing with traditional Chinese philosophy, this keynote invites global collaborators to advance practical, high-impact quantum solutions together.

title: Putting human rights into artificial intelligence
description: AI companies, such as Anthropic, have begun to think about the ethical implications of their transformative technologies by embedding a human rights respecting constitution into their AI. Should this approach become an industry standard to ensure that AI models adhere to the same moral and ethical standards as humans? Or should governments impose these standards from without?

This session challenges the myth of continuous optimisation, showing leaders how to design tools and working hour structures that give employees the mental space needed for breakthroughs.

George Aivazoglou, Managing Director of NBA Europe and Middle East, goes inside the NBA’s plans for Europe: a new competition, modern arenas, innovative partnerships and fan experiences built for a new generation. Hear how the league is making its move, and what it means for the game across the continent.

How do mainstream media outlets balance the demand for instant news without jeopardising editorial integrity? Join this panel of editorial leaders as they pull back the curtain on the high-stakes balancing act of maintaining absolute accuracy under absolute pressure.

growing education gap and why the private sector has both a responsibility and a strategic interest in helping to close it.

description: Meet Mudita and discover award-winning minimalist technology. Explore our E Ink phone, digital wellbeing products and partnership opportunities with our team. Ideal for retailers, distributors and industry partners.

description: AI assistants are only as good as the data behind them. In this live demo, we show how Statista Connect plugs verified market and consumer data straight into the AI tools teams already use: Claude, Microsoft 365 Copilot, ChatGPT and custom agents via MCP and API. Watch a single question become a sourced market sizing and a brand-funnel comparison in minutes.

title: The future of AI and machine learning
description: Over the course of an hour, startups explore the practical applications of AI and machine learning. Delve into real-world cases and gain insights into how these technologies are solving complex problems across diverse fields.

description: Discover how Qatar Science & Technology Park (QSTP) drives deep tech innovation, empowering startups, connecting industry and research, and accelerating growth through programs, partnerships and funding.

title: Silicon Valley vs. Europe and the race for global dominance
description: Global markets are in flux, forcing startups and VCs alike to adapt to a new economic reality. As funding landscapes realign, where will the next generation of industry disruptors originate? This session explores the changing dynamics between European and US tech ecosystems, looking at who is better positioned to lead the next growth cycle.

title: Are you making the right robotics decisions?
description: Stop by our stand and take the 5 minute the Robotics Readiness Challenge.  Make the calls that decide whether robotics scales: strategy, skills, safety, shape and scale. Find out if your decisions would deliver.

title: Building AI on your own terms: From technology discovery to real-world scale
description: Much of the world's current frontier AI capability is concentrated among a relatively small number of countries and technology providers, so how much control do nations and businesses have over their own AI future? This panel examines what it takes to move from AI dependency to greater control, covering infrastructure, technology and real-world scaling.

title: Solving the SMB cash crunch
description: SMBs power the global economy, yet traditional finance constantly leaves them stranded without reliable cash flow. While early fintech focused on flashy consumer apps and basic payments, a massive shift is underway. Fintech’s next groundbreaking era will solve the ultimate make-or-break hurdle for small business survival: cash flow.

title: The Portuguese economic success story
description: Portugal's economy has, despite unfavourable international headwinds, maintained strong growth. GDP per capita has increased for at least four straight years, unemployment is at an over ten-year low, and government debt continues to fall. We will hear from the Minister of Finance in charge of many of the reforms that have spurred this positive performance about how Portugal has gone from strength to strength.

timeslot_participations.name: Joaquim Miranda Sarmento
timeslot_participations.job_title: Minister of State and of Finance

title: Building the product isn’t the hard part. Building the company is.
description: When it comes to scaling climate tech, building great energy intelligence software is only the beginning. Drawing on his experience growing Watt Footprint from a startup into a global business, Paul Mahon explores what it takes to build the company behind the technology – from bringing together the right team and securing significant funding to shaping a strong culture and scaling sustainably.

title: Don’t feed shit to agents
description: Operating across 50+ global markets, LUSH built “The Vault” to turn fragmented product data into a single, governed source of truth. AI agents are only as good as their context. Feed an AI agent raw, unmodeled data and it fails. LUSH CTO Simon Ince and Directus co-founder & CTO Rijk van Zanten reveal how they engineered a governed data layer that gives both humans and AI the trusted context needed to build at scale.

title: Why AI agents stall at the production line
description: Open standards are missing in action, causing custom AI agents to fail when scaling. Join the AAIF's Mazin Gilbert as breaks down how open-source protocols eliminate proprietary lock-in and bridge the gap between impressive lab demos and reliable enterprise execution.

title: The next billion players will not download a game
description: Games used to be products people searched for and downloaded. AI is making games easier and cheaper to create, intensifying competition for players’ attention. The advantage is no longer just making great games, but ensuring they get discovered and building lasting relationships with players. Bozena Rezab, CEO and Co-founder of GAMEE, and David Brevik, President of Skystone Games, explore what happens to the gaming industry when anyone can make a game.

title: Building personal superintelligence: The future is for everyone
description: What happens when everyone has superintelligence in their hands? Join Meta's Derya Matras, VP, EMEA, on deploying AI that's personal, accessible, and built for everyone.

title: Game developers: Your next key hire
description: As AI reshapes skill requirements across industries, the games industry offers a growing pool of adaptable systems thinkers and creative problem solvers. With audience attention at a premium, are game developers the key to unlocking the next level of user engagement?

title: Taming token economics: A new framework for sustainable enterprise AI
description: Enterprises are racing to deploy generative AI and agents to lift productivity, yet face unpredictable, escalating token costs at scale. Uncontrolled token economics erodes expected efficiency gains and creates unplanned operational overhead. Explore a fresh architectural approach to balancing business value with cost predictability for large-scale AI deployment.

title: In bots we trust: Defending money against AI-powered fraud
description: Deepfakes, synthetic identities and instant payouts have supercharged fraud beyond traditional security. Stopping modern attacks takes custom AI models paired with behavioural signals, device data and human oversight. But as autonomous AI agents begin making transactions on our behalf, how do we protect trust at scale?

timeslot_participations.name: Ian Rogers
timeslot_participations.job_title: Chief Human Agency Officer & Board Member

title: Navigating today's AI landscape
description: Al is the most transformative technology we have ever seen, reshaping how technology companies are built and scaled, supercharging company creation and compressing the time it takes to reach major milestones. In this discussion, Philippe Botteri of Accel will cover how companies should approach the AI era, how AI is changing the return profile of traditional industries as the entire compute stack is being rewritten, and what the future could hold.

description: Public trust in mainstream media has fallen sharply across much of the West, as audiences question everything from editorial independence to the influence of governments, corporations and powerful interests. This talk explores whether this crisis of confidence is the result of misinformation, political polarisation, and social media? Or whether traditional journalism has lost credibility on its own terms?

timeslot_participations.name: Alan MacLeod

title: The key behavioral data that AI can finally reveal
description: InsideRisk’s AI-powered highly cinematic and customized simulations capture how people genuinely decide in real-life situations. The behavioral data is then used to assess, develop and train your workforce, with PII built in. Edouard Getaz, InsideRisk's Founder, will show you how some of the world's leading companies are adopting this groundbreaking approach.

title: Where venture value goes next
description: Foundation models were just the starting line. Drawing on Crunchbase's proprietary data across thousands of startups, Jager McConnell reveals where the next generation of venture value is actually being built. In this session, we'll discover why tomorrow's sustainable winners are abandoning shallow wrappers to build deep moats around unique data, specialised workflows, and defensible vertical expertise.

title: Building the next generation of humans [Hosted by Life With Artificials]
description:
AI, Robotics and Synthetic biology are enabling light speed developments in human enhancements. Join us in imagining what could future humans look like and do!
Please be aware that attendance is first-come, first-served.

title: $1.5 trillion in volume: Re-engineering a giant for the AI era
description: Running one of the world’s largest crypto exchanges requires moving beyond surface-level AI tools to fundamentally re-engineering how an enterprise operates. In this talk, Bybit CTO Rockman Zhang reveals the architectural blueprint of an AI-native crypto organization. He details how autonomous agents are used as an active execution layer across internal R&D and enterprise workflows. Learn how platforms can stay online 24/7 and safely handle non-stop trading as traditional finance and crypto merge.

title: Beyond the AI agent hype
description: AI has overinvested in producing intelligence and underinvested in determining where that intelligence deserves capital. This talk looks beyond the buzzwords to explore where AI agents are creating real economic value today, where they are not, and what it will take to turn increasingly capable AI into meaningful, scalable businesses especially as we approach what some describe as an “agentic singularity.”

title: Wind Down with Varun Vairavan
description: Stop by the HighLevel booth to meet and chat with Co-Founder Varun Vairavan, grab a FREE windbreaker, and connect with our team! Stick around until the end for your chance to win a FREE MacBook Neo in our exclusive giveaway! Must be present to win.

title: Why Valencia?

title: ✈️ Traveltech meetup
description: What's the next big shift in Traveltech? Debate it with peers who are living it 🚀. Connect with peers shaping the future of your field. Looking forward to seeing you!

title: Beyond the productivity paradox: The age of collaborative AI
description: Trillions are being invested in AI, yet many organisations are still struggling to translate adoption into meaningful productivity gains. Now, collaborative AI opens up a different frontier: not replacing human ingenuity, but amplifying it. CNTR CEO and Aleph Alpha Co-founder Jonas Andrulis demonstrates how a new kind of human-machine collaboration can unlock potential that neither humans nor AI can achieve alone.

title: From space missions to space infrastructure
description: The space industry is shifting from individual missions and bespoke systems toward scalable, interconnected infrastructure. Yet, unlocking its full potential requires overcoming challenges of scale and interoperability. This talk explains how shared, service-oriented infrastructure makes space accessible and commercially relevant. Drawing on SpaceComputer’s approach, explore how key management and secure computing become building blocks for space-enabled applications.

title: Speed Dating - Bring Us Your AI & Tech Challenge
description: Sit down 1:1 with a CONKORD expert, share a real business challenge and leave with a practical way forward, based on real projects.

description:
Are you a co-founder or thinking of becoming one? Join this honest conversation about navigating the highs and lows of building something together. Hear about the disagreements and power dynamics between co-founders in women-founded businesses.

This session is limited to 100 people, with spots available on a first-come, first-served basis.

title: 📣 Beyond the stage for growth leaders with Neha Mittal
description: Join Neha Mittal, Co-founder & CEO of JustAI, in a beyond the stage meetup on hypergrowth with a lean team. Founders and growth leaders: find out how small teams can grow faster than ever with AI, from someone who helped write the growth playbooks at Twitter and Pinterest ⚡ See you there!

title: AI sovereignty: Data control, governance and predictable AI costs [Hosted by Austriacard Holdings]
description: Explore what AI sovereignty means in practice and how organisations can run agentic AI on-premises, including in air-gapped environments. This session will cover data control, governance and approaches to managing AI costs, with GaiaB™ as a practical example. Please be aware that attendance is first-come, first-served.

timeslot_participations.job_title: Group Business Development Director, AI & Digital Solutions

title: Smart construction solutions
description: As the construction industry faces labour shortages, rising costs and site safety risks, Bright Master Robotics COO Zhao Nan explores how combining robotics with AI systems improves quality control and speeds up project delivery.

title: Who gets to design the future?
description: Mai Thi Nguyen, Director of the Design Lab at UC San Diego, explores how AI, design and civic technology can reshape the way cities work for the people who live in them. From housing and climate resilience to community engagement and public decision-making, she looks at how designers, technologists and communities can work together to build more inclusive, responsive and human-centred cities.

title: China’s global brand revolution
description: Chinese brands are making a bigger mark on markets around the world, from consumer technology and automotive to fashion and beauty. This keynote looks at the brands that have cracked the global market and the creative strategies behind their success, offering lessons that any brand can take from a new generation of global challengers.

title: Global Scaling Up Program Launch in Portugal, UAE, Brazil and US
description: Join us for the launch of the Global Scaling Up Programme, connecting innovation ecosystems across Portugal, the UAE, Brazil and the United States to support companies in their international growth.

title: From copilot to colleague: How AI agents join your team
description: Every team has an AI copilot, but few have an AI colleague. The difference? Colleagues know the context, own their work and get better every week without being asked twice. Drawing on lessons from building Strawberry Browser and helping teams put agents to work, Charles Maddock shares what it takes to bring agents onto the team and how leaders can build an AI-native team starting Monday.

title: Come Meet the Future of Leadership with LIA!
description:
We are pleased to invite Business, Operations, and HR leaders to join us for the official launch of LIA!

LIA is an AI leadership coach designed to support frontline leaders in navigating everyday challenges, making better decisions, and turning guidance into meaningful action.

We look forward to meet you and explore how LIA can support leadership development within your organisation.

title: The next financial crisis: Are we ready for what's coming?
description: With record public and private debt, geopolitical fragmentation and AI-driven market shifts, are the conditions for another financial crisis already in place? This talk examines the biggest risks facing the global financial system, from sovereign debt and central bank policy to asset bubbles, private credit, and geopolitical shocks. Our panel will debate whether today's economy is fundamentally more resilient than in 2008, or whether we're simply waiting for the next trigger.

timeslot_participations.name: James Galbraith

title: What happens when AI replaces your CEO?
description: What happens when you replace Executive planning and decision making with AI systems built on World Models and Recursive Self-Improvement (RSI)? Join Sam Pasupalak, Co-founder & CEO of Skyfall AI, as he explores building the new frontier — AI that can autonomously learn and operate SaaS businesses like an “AI CEO". What does this entail for the future of humanity?

title: The 10-person company with a 1, 000-person attack surface
description: AI lets a 10-person team run what once took 1, 000 people and lets attackers probe all of it just as cheaply. Security can no longer scale with headcount, so Tolmo's Arnaud Breton lays out how lean teams can stay secure while shipping 10x faster at AI speed.

title: AI technology made in Germany: The hows & whats
description: Panel on German AI technology.

title: Approaching the frictionless enterprise
description: The biggest bottleneck to organisational growth is rarely strategy, but the internal friction. When marketing speed outpaces HR policy or governance structures slow down market execution, performance stalls. This cross-disciplinary session examines the framework for modern team dynamics that can drive rapid execution in an unpredictable market.

title: Shifting foundations with automation: AI workflows keeping companies aloft
description: AI and automation are shifting the foundations of global corporate efficiency, digital commerce and venture scale. This session discusses how to orchestrate complex workflows across physical and digital marketplaces to accelerate growth without sacrificing data sovereignty or infrastructure stability.

title: Is traditional banking broken? And can it be fixed?
description: While most banks use AI for basic customer support, bunq is rebuilding core financial experiences around generative models. Join CSO Bianca Zwart to learn how Europe’s second-largest neobank uses native GenAI to eliminate financial admin friction and deliver truly autonomous banking.

title: When AI verifies AI
description: Traditional software follows strict rules: input A always equals output B. AI is different. It improvises, adapts, and sometimes makes things up. When an app never gives the exact same answer twice, how do you guarantee it stays accurate and safe? Join TestMu AI's Asad Khan as he breaks down how teams use smart AI testing tools to catch hallucinated facts, stress-test security, and keep customer-facing AI on the rails.

title: Less is more: AI's next race is efficiency
description: The first AI cycle was defined by scale: bigger models, more compute, and unprecedented infrastructure. The next cycle will increasingly be defined by who can make AI more efficient and accessible across the stack. Rocio Wu of F-Prime breaks down the AI stack from the ground up, from energy grids and cooling systems to chip design and smart software, to show where the biggest bottlenecks are today. As the industry opens up and becomes more competitive, the next major winners will be those who can deliver smart results with fewer resources.

title: The biggest buyout in history was a games company
description: EA has just gone private in a $55bn deal, the largest LBO ever. It marks a defining moment for gaming: its biggest franchises are no longer just cultural phenomena, but some of the world’s most valuable creative properties. This panel brings together the people financing game IP, the founders who built and sold it, and the operators running studios through change. What are people really buying when a game world changes hands? Can financial backing coexist with creative ambition, player trust and long-term investment?

title: Open vs closed: The debate defining the AI era
description: As AI becomes a defining technology of the 21st century, a fundamental divide exists in how it is developed, shared and controlled. Broadly speaking, actors in China and the West are pursuing different strategies: open source collaboration vs proprietary models. This talk explores the strategic, economic, and political drivers behind openness versus control, including national security concerns, innovation incentives, and global competitiveness.

Join this meetup to learn from Bernardo Seixas, CEO of Granter, about how his team created the perfect pitch that got them to win Web Summit PITCH competition 2025. Bring questions, practice your pitch, and get ready for live feedback!

title: An AI development partner with you in the driver seat [Hosted by IBM]
description: AI coding assistants are everywhere, but most were built for individual developers, not the enterprise. As teams move from vibe coding to agentic engineering, the stakes rise around quality, control, and cost. In this session, we’ll map the AI coding agent landscape, look at what makes a tool enterprise-ready, and show how IBM Bob is built to help teams ship faster without giving up control. Please be aware that attendance is first-come, first-served.

description: Shoppers expect stores to know what they want. Personalized search, recommendations, promotions and content can raise conversion and average order value without adding manual work. A Solution Engineer will demo live how VTEX adapts the experience to each shopper in real time.

title: The future of money
description: Dive into the future of fintech, and learn how everything from digital banking and online lending to robo-advisory services are reshaping the financial landscape. Explore how financial tools, cryptocurrencies, and blockchain transactions are playing their part in democratising finance, boosting inclusion, and enhancing customer experiences.

title: Beyond better: how brands reshape and make categories
description: What happens when the question your industry has always answered is no longer the right one? For years, being better was the game. Now the brands that matter most are the ones willing to ask something different. Wolff Olins’ Global CEO Sairah Ashman explores how brands reshape and make categories, and what it takes to stop racing to win inside a frame you never chose.

title: Your AI doesn't know your market, and here's how to fix that
description: When enterprises today ask AI for market strategy, web-trained models yield the same generic answers. To unlock precise, high-stakes decisions, Rwazi’s Kapil Mathrani introduces a three-layer approach combining internal company data, macro-market trends and first-party behavioural data shared voluntarily by five million consumers. Discover how combining these layers delivers precise insights and why transparent data collection is key to outputs you can actually trust.

title: The robotic front desk
description: Front-of-house hospitality is shifting away from static check-in desks and tablet screens. Join Botifull founder Maxime LeBerre to see an autonomous receptionist robot designed for hotels, retail and modern offices. Discover how embodied AI handles guest greetings, access triage and client interactions, turning traditional reception into an efficient service hub.

title: What replaces the click?
description: AI consumes the web’s best reporting and creative work, answers the query, and starves the creator of traffic and revenue. Having invented the pay-per-click model that funded the internet, ProRata.ai founder Bill Gross outlines the next commercial architecture of the web: embedding direct attribution and micropayments into frontier models before original digital publishing goes extinct.

title: Most companies don't need AI engineers, and here's why
description: When companies ask for an AI engineer, what they often need is something else: a data or automation problem that a different profile would solve faster and at a lower cost. Jaime Castillo, co-founder and chief revenue officer of Shakers, shares what he has learned working with more than 600 companies across Europe: the new roles the AI era is creating, why diagnosing before hiring saves months and how a global consultancy went from one project to more than 60 without rebuilding its team.

title: Give me a brake: Coding without crashing
description: When AI is generating code at 100 miles an hour, who is really in control? Moving fast is exhilarating, but without a dependable emergency brake, you're accelerating toward a 3 a.m. outage. Defined.ai founder and CEO Daniela Braga shows how high-quality training data prevents bad model habits before they reach your codebase, while LaunchDarkly co-founder & CEO Edith Harbaugh demonstrates how feature flags and runtime controls keep engineers firmly in the driver's seat.

title: The new financing frontier: How intellectual property unlocks capital
description: Turning ideas into growth at scale remains a challenge for startups and businesses across Europe. How can IP-backed finance unlock a new source of capital? This session explores the opportunity, the barriers to scaling IP-backed finance and the market and regulatory changes needed to turn Europe’s intellectual property into investable capital.

title: Banking anywhere but the bank
description: A bank is a bundle of businesses: holding money, moving it, lending it and growing it. Today, each of those businesses can run on its own licence, in any market, without a banking licence. Ridwan Olalere, co-founder and CEO of LemFi, breaks down the P&L of a typical bank to show how financial services are being rebuilt and why AI will make the bank itself the least important part of banking.

title: Maintaining the human in an AI world
description: As AI and algorithms increasingly shape how people navigate the world, genuine human connection has never been more sought after or more valuable. Reddit COO Jen Wong explores why the next era of the internet will depend not on more information, but on trusted context, personal opinion and firsthand experience, considering how authentic human dialogue can strengthen AI, search & discovery while keeping people at the centre of an increasingly automated internet.

title: You did everything right. Now what?
description: Study hard, master your craft, build a career, get that promotion. That was the deal. But as AI enables machines to do more of our work, what happens to the identities we've built around it? We bring together a founder building autonomous companies, a venture investor and an interfaith minister to explore how technology is changing work, and the choices we may finally have to make for ourselves.

title: How do you build creative ambition?
description: Creativity can be trained. But how do you unlock it in others? Luiza Baffa, Head of Creative Studio at On, in conversation with Jean Rosier, Partner & CCO of Perestroika, explore how we build creative confidence and ambition, from developing our own creative muscles to creating environments where people feel empowered to experiment, take risks and do their best work.

title: Sourcing, signals and the future of deal flow
description: How do you find the next $100B startup when everyone is looking in the same places? From corporate intelligence networks and global pitch engines to algorithmic deal flow, top VCs are rewriting their sourcing playbooks. In this session, we discuss how leading investors cut through market noise and back tomorrow's category leaders before the rest of the market catches on.

title: HealthHub Open Innovation: Show Up Before the Problem Does
description: Discover how open innovation is helping address healthcare challenges. Meet leading industry partners and the three winning startups showcasing innovative solutions shaping the future of healthcare.

title: The perks of loyalty: How embedded rewards turn everyday spending into revenue
description: Loyalty has shifted from a cost centre to a core revenue driver, where integration speed matters far more than reward size. Drawing on more than 30 white-label implementations across Europe, Finperks' Sebastian Seifert explores why one embedded product fits three different industries – banks, fintechs and HR SaaS platforms. Discover what actually gets business cases signed, why implementation speed beats price in closing deals and how to compress launch timelines from months to weeks.

title: Beyond the bans: Protecting youth rights in a fragmented online world
description: Across Europe and beyond, governments are racing to regulate childrens' access to the internet with age verification mandates, platform bans, screen-time restrictions, and different sets of national rules that rarely align with one another. But as the policy landscape fragments, the question must be asked: how can governments and privacy agencies better align to ensure the safety of kids and prevent the access to problematic content being confined to the darker corners of the internet.

In this keynote, Andi Blattmann explores how Black Forest Labs is building the foundation of this next layer of intelligence, and how this foundation enables the next generation of physical AI.

Brooke Hopkins, founder & CEO of Coval and former lead engineer who built evaluation infrastructure for self-driving cars at Waymo, draws on her lessons to help teams set rigorous benchmarks, ship zero-tolerance voice agents, and build self-improving safety loops.

title: AI's next billion-dollar market

title: Scaling what cannot be standardized

title: What happens if open source wins?

title: Are we just tokenising a broken system?

title: Governing the shadows: Emerging risks in non-bank finance
description: Shadow banking, or non-bank financial intermediation, has become a vital source of funding for the technology sector while reshaping global finance. This talk examines the governance of asset managers, hedge funds and other non-bank institutions, asking whether existing oversight is fit for purpose. Drawing on lessons from the 2008 financial crisis and recent market shocks, it explores accountability, debt management, and the systemic risks at the core of an increasingly interconnected financial system.

title: The fast and the curious
description: In an economy driven by technological change, static training modules and annual re-skilling programmes are no longer enough. A key determinant of enterprise survival is the speed at which an organisation learns, adapts and converts new knowledge into execution. This session explores how to build an architecture of continuous adaptation across your workforce.

title: The best offense is a machine-speed defence
description: As AI reshapes technology, one truth holds: innovation can only move as fast as the security protecting it. The same AI empowering defenders is supercharging attackers at machine speed. CrowdStrike CEO and Founder George Kurtz explores why security is the foundation of the AI era, letting business move faster and safer. From cloud networks to split-second Formula 1 data, see why the companies that win with AI are the ones that secure it first.

title: What 10, 000 hours of challenger brand research reveals about the future of growth
description: Over five years and 10, 000 hours of research, Rival has run the most comprehensive studies of challenger brands in the world. In partnership with Imperial College, the Rival 50 Index screens more than 5, 000 challenger brands every year to identify the top 50 redefining the modern marketing playbook. In this session Eric Fulwiler, CEO of Rival, will reveal the Rival 50 of 2026 and the key insights and takeaways on the future of brand and positioning.

title: Brazil's blueprint for cyber resilience
description: Cyber threats are redefining national security. When every critical service relies on cloud infrastructure, how can nations ensure control without retreating into digital isolation? Drawing on Brazil’s real-world rollout of sovereign cloud infrastructure, Wilton Mota will explore why sovereignty is becoming a fundamental pillar of cybersecurity and how governments can achieve operational autonomy.

title: Hormones as the next frontier of women’s longevity and healthspan
description: Women spend 25% more of their lives in poor health than men, yet female-specific conditions receive just 1% of non-oncology research. This talk explores how continuous, non-invasive hormone monitoring turns an overlooked blind spot into actionable data, opening a new market for personalised and accessible healthcare and laying the groundwork for world models of human health. Clair Health’s 22-year-old founder shares how she built the scientific rigour and consumer trust needed to raise an $11.6M seed round for the first non-invasive continuous hormone-monitoring wearable and the opportunity ahead.

title: Betting on people: Building the opportunity economy
description: The next era of the creator economy will be defined by the companies willing to invest in the people behind the work. Eric Wittman, CEO of VSCO, explores the power of backing individuals, supporting artists and creating real opportunities for creators to thrive. From putting photographers at the centre of its community to supporting them in the physical world, he explores how investing in people can build a creator economy that works for both creators and the businesses behind them.

description: China’s rise as an industrial and technological powerhouse raises an important question for Europe: what can we learn from its approach? From EVs, batteries and solar power to high-speed rail and robotics, China has achieved remarkable scale and speed. This talk explores what Europe can learn from China’s industrial strategy, investment and approach to technological competitiveness.

title: Is AI flattening the tech market or concentrating it?
description: The lopsided market conditions have kept everyone wondering for some time now; is there a bubble, and what happens next? Simply ‘investing in AI’ is not a sustainable strategy. Mattias Ljungman of Moonfire Ventures offers a concrete view of what constitutes long-term value when nothing seems certain.

title: A new era of human-computer interaction
description: What if a pair of glasses could transform how we see, hear and connect with the world? Join Irene Long, CSO at Rokid, to explore how AI glasses are breaking down barriers, empowering industries, enriching everyday life and making the world more accessible.

title: Public Capital. Private Ambition. Global Impact.
description: How does Portugal Ventures and BPF Group's ecosystem bring together complementary financing solutions to support business growth, maximizing economic impact for Portugal.

title: The instant economy: Why are we still waiting for our own money?
description: Despite real-time rails and instant settlement capabilities, everyday finance remains bound by legacy schedules. This discussion examines the shift to instant payments, earned wage access, and how real-time money movement impacts risk, regulation, and consumer flexibility.

title: Beyond software: Mastering end-to-end industrial AI
description: The future competitiveness of European industry won't be decided by who builds the fastest AI prototype, but by who masters combining physical hardware, embedded AI, UX and sovereign cloud infrastructure into market-ready, scalable products. Join us in discussing how European mid-market leaders and OEMs can bridge the gap from product strategy on the factory floor to resilient edge-and-cloud architecture.

title: The new rules of audience development
description: The strongest media businesses understand that audience development and business development are deeply connected. This talk examines how data, editorial insight, community building, and experimentation can help media organisations understand who their audiences are, and more importantly, what those audiences need. It explores how deeper audience relationships can drive loyalty, growth, and new commercial opportunities.

title: The new battle for brand influence
description: The path from discovery to purchase is being reshaped by platforms, creators, brands and AI. This panel explores how marketers are adapting as the places where people discover products, make decisions and transact increasingly overlap, and what brands need to do to stay relevant and trusted along the way.

title: The next shift: People, AI, and the future of work
description: The next era of work demands more than new technology. It calls for a new approach to skills, jobs, and opportunity. What if some of the most important skills of tomorrow are the ones we've relied on for generations? Hear from Amazon's VP of HR on rethinking investments in people, from AI skills to hands-on trades, and preparing a global workforce of more than 1 million people for the next era of work.

title: Follow the algorithm to see where capital moves next
description: Software ate the world... now it is devouring global finance. This session explores where capital is actually flowing today, who holds the keys to tomorrow’s liquidity, and what happens when software becomes the primary allocator of global wealth.

Every coding agent knows your code. Almost none of them know your work, the Jira issue that kicked it off, the Confluence doc that explains the trade-offs, the decisions made last sprint, or the team that owns the outcome. The result: agents that sound confident and build the wrong thing.

We'll show you the difference. Live. Side-by-side.

title: Can you promise a delivery date you’re sure you can keep?
description: An accurate delivery promise makes the sale and keeps the customer coming back. When that promise ignores stock, carrier limits or warehouse capacity, it turns into a broken promise. In this session, a Solution Engineer will show how VTEX uses real-time inventory, logistics rules and delivery capacity to calculate dates that are both reliable and competitive.

title: AI as an employee in your organization
description: Automate what you’ve done thousands of times and do more with the team you already have. We’ll explore the AI philosophy behind this: use AI as an employee, not just a bot. We’ll discuss how to rely on AI to handle complex operational tasks where time and precision matter, and how to integrate AI agents as employees into everyday workflows across teams.

title: The athlete advantage
description: Today's athletes are building brands, investing in businesses and using their platforms to create meaningful change. Belgium's record international and founder Jan Vertonghen, APEX's Koen Bosma to explore how athletes are turning their experiences, influence and ideas into new ventures and social impact.

title: Capital beyond equity
description: Europe’s emerging AI hardware, robotics and industrial automation sectors require massive upfront capex, yet traditional venture capital is ill-equipped to fund physical infrastructure. Bringing together deep tech investors, robotics founders and debt infrastructure pioneers, this session explores the financial mechanics needed to fund Europe’s reindustrialisation, without surrendering founder equity.

title: Beyond the logo: The real value of an F1 partnership
description: Formula 1 is the fastest-growing sport in the world – and every brand wants to get involved. But the hard part is creating value beyond the grid. This session unpacks lessons from building one of the sport's biggest partnerships, revealing what makes sponsorships compound over time, why logo and hospitality aren’t enough, and how brands can turn an F1 partnership into a lasting growth engine.

title: How does patient capital accelerate innovation and technology?
description: Patience sounds like the opposite of speed. In deep tech, it’s often what makes speed possible. Kim Chong, Chief Risk Officer at the Hong Kong Investment Corporation Limited, explains how long-term capital speeds innovation up: it frees founders to build, carries innovative breakthroughs from lab to market, and brings market long term capital in behind them.

title: Political influence and the algorithm: Who sets the rules?
description: Join Open to Debate as Renée DiResta and Aidan Kohn-Murphy examine how digital content is fundamentally altering democratic accountability and political engagement. Together, they’ll debate a defining question of our digital age: should government set rules for algorithms on social media?

title: Is quantum the next frontier of the AI race?
description: Can quantum technologies deliver the acceleration silicon no longer can? Join quantum industry leaders as they debate where quantum acceleration genuinely matters for AI, and confront the harder question: is quantum a decisive edge in the AI race, or a parallel track defining its own?

title: Rewriting the rules of female longevity
description: Women’s health has long been approached in fragments, often reactive and disconnected, leaving major gaps in how women understand their bodies and navigate different stages of life. This session introduces a new product that brings together health intelligence, personalization and technology to help women take a more proactive role in living healthier for longer. What could a new approach to female longevity look like?

title: The path to processing US$10bn in payments
description: Compliance cannot be a bottleneck if you want to scale, and regulation has to be approached as a partnership, not an obstacle. Bernardo shares how building local banking relationships market by market, rather than trying to route around them, turned Trace Finance into core infrastructure for four of the world's largest payment providers operating in LatAm.

title: The mask in the mirror
description: As AI learns to imitate us, what decides who we become? As the face of DeepTomCruise and co-founder of Metaphysic, Miles Fisher has experienced synthetic identity from the inside, amassing over 5 million TikTok followers and 500 million views. In a funny, personal and visually compelling talk, he asks what happens when AI can convincingly manufacture almost anything, and argues that the scarce human skill will not be authenticity, but authorship.

title: The autonomous enterprise: Networks, cloud and AI agents
description: Networks, cloud infrastructure and AI are converging to change how companies operate and how customers interact with digital services. As networks become more autonomous, organisations face both new opportunities and challenges. Join us in exploring practical applications that can improve customer and business experiences while developing and scaling AI agents.

title: Women's health is a $1 trillion blindspot
description: For decades women’s health was treated as a niche market—yet women control 80% of healthcare decisions and represent a trillion-dollar market gap. This session bridges the gap between high-level venture capital, digital health deployment, privacy-first AI models and brand storytelling that breaks cultural taboos.

title: Viable systems, judgement, and AI safety
description: This talk explores how the Good Regulator Theorem can guide safe AI delegation, highlighting that AI agents excel at data processing and algorithmic accounting. However, building truly safe and viable systems requires preserving human judgment, authority, and, ultimate responsibility.

title: Leading Mobility Innovation in the Region of Lisbon
description: Explore how innovation is shaping the future of mobility in the Lisbon region. Discover new approaches, opportunities and partnerships driving more connected and sustainable mobility solutions.

title: Why smart enterprises keep buying broken AI promises
description: Smart enterprises invest heavily in AI only to struggle with adoption and fractured integrations. Backed by $100M to fix that gap, Unframe co-founder Larissa outlines what software buyers get wrong, and how to turn existing systems into high-impact AI powerhouses from day one.

description: Join IBM's Sarah Meron and Scuderia Ferrari ambassador Marc Gené for the announcement of the IBM Sports Tech Startup Prize Competition winner.

A focused coffee meetup for CTOs, founders, product leaders, and innovation teams exploring how to move AI initiatives from prototype to production without long hiring cycles.

description: Think you know where your startup really stands? Experience Source Code. Pinpoint your stage, see what needs attention, explore your personalized Blueprint and ongoing guidance, and make your next move. Please be aware that attendance is first-come, first-served.

title: When software meets matter
description: Generating text and code is frictionless compared to moving through physical space. The next decade belongs to physical AI: software that leaves the safety of the browser to interact directly with kinetic reality. Operating outside the data center demands what language models could never deliver – spatial depth, continuous motion, and immediate physical consequence. This session breaks down the architecture of embodied autonomy, exploring how next-generation world models turn raw algorithms into machines that can safely navigate the physical universe.

title: Investing in technological sovereignty: EU funding for your project [Hosted by European Health and Digital Executive Agency (HaDEA)]
description: Join HaDEA’s workshop to discover EU funding opportunities for your next project. Learn how EU funding is supporting technological sovereignty, meet representatives of the European Commission and get inspired by EU-funded projects. Please be aware that attendance is first-come, first-served.

title: How to Scale Your Business Beyond Your Current Market
description: Find ways and opportunities to expand your business internationally, enter new markets, and build strategic partnerships. We'll discuss practical strategies for overcoming market entry challenges, hiring global talent, and navigating international workforce compliance to support sustainable business growth.

timeslot_participations.job_title: Founder and Ecosystem builder in diverse Markets

title: Is VC playing it too safe?
description: Venture capital was built to fund the impossible, yet a decade of cheap capital has turned it into a consensus-driven machine chasing safe metrics. Outsized returns require solitary conviction. Join this session as we move past the hype to explore the true mechanics of contrarian investing, finding non-obvious opportunities, and spotting frontier markets years before they become obvious.

title: Front-end developer meetup
description: Calling all front-end developers! Join this meetup to share workflows, exchange technical insights, and grow your network
