title: 🎮 Gamers, AR & VR meetup
description: What's the next big shift in Gaming, AR & VR? Debate it with peers who are living it 🚀. Connect with peers shaping the future of your field. Looking forward to seeing you!

title: Nomads with roots: The ecosystem of the future
description: Technology has made the world a smaller place. We can travel, communicate, and interact across continents in a matter of minutes. These changes present myriad challenges for those building communities rooted in a particular location, but they also present immense opportunities. In this panel we hear from seasoned ecosystem builders about how to craft a thriving community of technology builders, in a world of digital nomads.

title: SÃO PAULO meets the World
description: Meet startups from across the State and City of São Paulo, Brazil, taking innovation global and representing Latin America’s most dynamic innovation ecosystem. Connect with founders and leaders in a session by the São Paulo State Secretariat for Science, Technology and Innovation, InvestSP, the state's investment promotion agency, and ADE SAMPA, the city's development agency.

title: Send, scale, reinvent: how to keep building after product-market fit
description: LemFi co-founder and CEO Ridwan shares how the company scaled from a remittance product into a global financial platform serving more than two million customers. Ridwan unpacks the growth decisions behind LemFi’s journey, from raising significant funding and entering investing to integrating stablecoin settlement rails through partnerships with Tether and BVNK.

title: Who shapes US foreign policy?
description: In money driven electoral systems, campaign finance can play a disproportionate role in public policy outcomes. In this talk Eli Clifton discusses his new book Israel’s Lobby: America in the Grip of a Foreign Power. He explores how lobbying, campaign finance, and elite influence have evolved and why the relationship between the US and Israel has become one of the most consequential and contested issues in American politics.

title: When AI meets the physical world
description: AI is no longer confined to screens and software. As connectivity, sensors and intelligent systems become more embedded in business and cities, companies are beginning to rethink how operations can be monitored, automated and optimised in real time. Join us in discussing how companies can move from collecting data to using it to make physical operations safer, smarter and more autonomous.

title: Earth data for enterprise: The key to next-level growth
description: As AI moves into enterprise workflows, success will depend not just on models, but on the quality, scale and accessibility of the data behind them. In this session, AI and data infrastructure leaders will explore where current data pipelines fall short, how to make real-world data accessible to AI and agentic systems, and what becomes possible when data, infrastructure and models work together.

title: Is the AI bubble already bursting?
description: Investors have priced a lot of good news into AI, but real-world spending data tells a more complicated story. Ramp economist Ara Kharazian tracks business spending to reveal hidden weak spots, vendor concentration, and market risks. Join Ara as he puts the AI thesis under pressure to test what might already be going wrong. Bring your phone to participate in live audience voting at the start and end of the session.

timeslot_participations.name: Ara Kharazian
timeslot_participations.job_title: Lead Economist and Head of Economics Lab

timeslot_participations.name: Luke Vargas
timeslot_participations.job_title: Podcast Host of WSJ's What's News

title: SPUR Coalition: The fight to save the news industry
description: The news media industry is arguably the most exposed industry to technology. Artificial intelligence in particular is upending its business models, the role of the journalist and changing information ecosystems. For the first time ever, media groups have banded together to form the SPUR Coalition which sets out rules, standards and AI infrastructure for how the media works and AI companies will work together. This panel brings together executives from three founding member groups, Sky News, Associated Press, and The Financial Times to discuss how this growing coalition of the world's top news organisations plan to evolve and protect the industry as a whole from prevailing and unregulated tech forces.

timeslot_participations.name: Matthew Rogerson
timeslot_participations.job_title: Director of Global Public Policy & Platform Strategy

title: Powering the backbone
description: When scaling critical tech, how do market leaders navigate bottlenecks when real-world constraints, local compliance, and regulatory frameworks refuse to move as fast as software? Join Stilta CEO Oskar Block, Seltz AICEO this session as industry leaders debate true operational resilience when building infrastructure that powers the global economy.

title: Vivaldi v Goliath: The case for sovereign code
description: From the creator of Opera and CEO of Vivaldi, Jon von Tetzchner comes a counter-trend masterclass in web ethics. While big tech rushes to embed AI into every application, Vivaldi intentionally avoids integrating AI into the browser to protect data privacy. Learn why Europe needs to construct its own independent web infrastructure to maintain digital sovereignty, and how this privacy-first philosophy is putting Vivaldi at the frontier of a market that did not exist before.

title: Can a tech company grow by getting people off its app?
description: What happens when success means your customers leave? This conversation explores the business behind building something designed to be deleted, and how helping people build relationships shapes product decisions, earns trust and drives growth. As AI changes how people meet and communicate, we will examine which parts of connecting technology can improve, which require human effort, and what other businesses can learn from building around what happens after someone closes the app.

title: The enterprise reality check: Who’s controlling data and AI?
description: Everyone feels in control until disruption exposes the cracks. As AI systems become more powerful and technology ecosystems more interconnected, enterprises are being forced to confront a difficult reality: can they prove their digital sovereignty and control of the technology their business depends on? IBM will debut exclusive research exploring the gap between confidence and capability, uncovering what failure could cost, where organizations are most vulnerable, and what separates true digital sovereignty leaders from those whose control was never as strong as they believed.

timeslot_participations.name: Jonathan Adashek
timeslot_participations.job_title: Senior Vice President and Chief Global Affairs Officer

title: The only skills that matter now
description: As AI automates routine knowledge work, companies are redefining what they value in talent. Drawing on market data from executive search and Europe’s largest freelance platform, Dan Porter and Malt CEO Vincent Huguet explore what the modern workforce requires. description: After years of subdued activity, the technology IPO market is showing signs of a revival. A new generation of high-growth companies (e.g Anthropic) are considering going public. But what is driving the new IPO boom and are valuations justified? Financial experts Patrick Boyle and Adam Kobeissi examine the forces behind the IPO revival, the companies preparing to take the plunge, and whether this new wave represents genuine opportunity, or irrational exuberance.

title: The next chapter of storytelling
description: From global TV formats and streaming hits to bestselling novels, comics and video games, storytelling is no longer confined to a single screen or medium. Academy Award-nominated producer & founder of Blue Hour Pictures, Ashley Schlaifer, Co-founder & CEO of Avail, Chris Giliberti and Margaret Stohl, bestselling author and screenwriter, explore how stories are being created, expanded and experienced across platforms, and what it takes to build worlds and characters that connect with audiences in a rapidly changing entertainment landscape.

title: Code, conscience and the whistleblower
description: You submitted the ticket, warned product managers and flagged the issue, but the product is shipping anyway. When normal workplace channels break down, what comes next? This session provides a practical roadmap for technical staff caught between conscience and career. Attendees will learn how independent support communities protect engineers and how to document concerns responsibly. Crucially, they will discover why developers refusing to deploy reckless code is our final line of defence against an unchecked AI future.

title: The data behind the next viral sensation
description: What if you could spot the next breakout creator before anyone else? Rohan Kumar helped build one of MrBeast's fastest-growing accounts using proprietary creator data from Kyra. Now, alongside Kyra's Devran Karaca, he'll unpack how identifying outliers, understanding audience growth and pairing data with big creative ideas can give creators and brands an edge.

title: Agents don't need prompts, they need context

Serial founder and product leader Milkana Brace explores how building a continuous context layer bridges the gap between human creativity and autonomous execution at scale.

title: The last days of the rules-based order?
description: Wars, great-power rivalry and competing visions of sovereignty are putting the international legal system under extraordinary strain. In this talk, Mary Robinson, Henry Farrell, and Victor Gao ask whether the rules-based order is entering a period of fundamental transformation and what, if anything, could replace it.

StoReel co-founder and co-CEO Angela Yu explains why AI entertainment, gaming and content are merging: characters you can talk to, plots you can steer, worlds audiences help shape. And how do you scale a format that’s still being invented?

title: Metrics that matter: From AI benchmarks to EBITDA
description: Strong AI benchmarks have raised expectations, but turning technical capability into company-level results takes more than deploying a model. Hops, Wrike and Zencoder founder Andrew Filev explores how enterprises can turn individual AI productivity gains into business acceleration, examining the governance, culture and processes needed to build repeatable workflows grounded in deep human-AI collaboration.

title: The new battleground in the AI race

Join Cerebras Systems Chief Strategy Officer Andy Hock to explore how ultra-fast inference is powering the next generation of AI applications.

This provided the US safe cover for meddling in the affairs of countries whose policies it did not approve of whilst evading direct responsibility. With the shuttering of USAID, has America decided to limit foreign interference or put global human rights below the list of priorities? Here to discuss this and more is Mike Benz, formerly of the State Department now head of the Foundation for Freedom Online.

title: From missing sunlight to a growth story
description: Researchers spend years in the lab on R&D projects but often fail to turn even groundbreaking science into validated, scalable health technology. Leading cognitive scientists and frontier researchers are abandoning corporate tech giants to build agile, hypothesis-driven labs pursuing fundamentally new bets. Join Prosper's Danielle Perszyk for an unvarnished look at the splintering of the AI establishment, exposing the scientific divisions, structural divergence, and architectural debates separating the new generation of research labs from legacy cloud incumbents.

What happens when the website itself becomes an agent, able to understand intent and shape the experience around whoever, or whatever, shows up? Jonathan Arena, co-founder and CEO of New Generation, makes the case for a web built for both humans and AI, and explores what happens when the page stops being the starting point.

title: What does "new" even mean?
description: For decades, commerce has been built around the idea that new is better. But resale is challenging how we think about newness, ownership, affordability and value. Using Vinted as a case study, this talk asks whether the next era of commerce can create growth not only by making more things, but by unlocking more value from the things that already exist.

title: Built to last: The reinvention and reimagining of iconic brands
description: The most enduring brands aren’t the ones that stay the same. They're the ones that evolve without losing what people love about them. As a new CMCO taking a fresh look at one of marketing’s most iconic platforms – Priceless – Jill Kramer explores how marketers can balance consistency with innovation, stay relevant to new generations of consumers, and ensure their most valuable brand assets remain powerful for decades to come.

title: Beyond the IPO: The new exit playbook
description: Going public isn't the only way to win anymore. With the secondary market exploding, companies are staying private longer than ever. So how do founders and investors actually get paid? This session explores the new reality of exits, what it means for the IPO, and where capital is heading next.

title: Reimagining reproduction: Evolution by genetic optimisation
description: Nucleus founder and CEO Kian Sadeghi shows that what was once science fiction - having a taller, smarter, healthier baby - can now be done at any IVF clinic around the world. Building on his recent book he argues that a new kind of evolution is here, one directed by you. Whereas natural selection has reproductive success as the ultimate goal, evolution by genetic optimisation has human flourishing.

title: Pricing the physical world

Lighthouse’s Sean Fitzpatrick and Pony.ai’s Leo Wang compare how each business forecasts demand, sets prices, and keeps its assets in use. Both build software that decides how physical assets get used. They’ll unpack how to serve radically different customers, where forecasts fall short, and what SaaS can learn from it.

title: Connecting the bots: Building secure infrastructure for inter-agent communication
description: As AI agents quickly become your primary users and customers, inter-bot traffic is surging. Yet, getting autonomous agents to communicate securely with each other remains a major unsolved bottleneck. Primitive founder Ethan Byrd breaks down how to build secure communication layers that unlock massive scale while protecting your underlying systems.

title: The next leap in intelligence: From generating content to understanding the world
description: AI can conjure entire worlds from a single prompt. So why bother capturing the one we already live in？Imagination isn't the same as truth. When a robot has to navigate a factory, when a city plans its next decade, when a film rebuilds a real place, a beautiful hallucination isn't good enough. These systems need the physical world measured, not guessed. This talk makes the case for spatial intelligence built on real-world data: 3D reconstruction that turns physical spaces into accurate, reusable digital assets. AI gives machines imagination. Spatial intelligence gives them a world worth trusting.

title: Live Podcast: The Interface
description: From AI and influencers to memes, data leaks, cybersecurity and the weirdest corners of the web, The Interface explores what happens when technology collides with real life. Cutting through the hype, the hosts unpack the platforms, products and online phenomena that increasingly shape our choices, our culture and our sense of self - whether we like it or not!

title: The ethical alternatives to big tech
description: Our lives in the modern world have become increasingly dominated by a small number of enormous companies, that each wield an unprecedented amount of power. Too often they use this power to trample on our rights and restrict our freedoms. In this talk we hear from a man leading the fight back against big tech about how to build ethical alternatives to the tools that have come to dominate our lives.

title: How podcasting rewired the talent deal
description: Traditionally media outlets owned the content produced and talent got a salary or a fee but this has been replaced by something closer to a joint venture. This talk traces how podcasting made that shift possible, why hosts increasingly hold IP and equity stakes instead of just appearance fees, and what legacy and new outlets alike are having to renegotiate to keep top talent in the building.

title: Dream big: How creativity drives growth

Join Marcel Marcondes, AB InBev’s Global Chief Marketing Officer, and Anselmo Ramos, Co-Founder and Chief Creative Officer of GUT, to learn how AB InBev capitalizes on creativity, technology, and innovation to deliver consistent, compounding growth. As the first three-time winner of the Cannes Lions Creative Marketer of the Year, Marcel and Anselmo share how AB InBev uses marketing capabilities to solve business and consumer problems.

title: The next AI race is physical: From prototype to productivity
description: AI is moving off the screen and into the physical world, from robotic arms on factory floors to flying robots with dexterous hands. This panel explores what it takes to turn prototypes into productivity, whether general-purpose or specialised machines will win, and how China’s mix of AI research, manufacturing depth and rapid iteration is shaping the next frontier of physical AI.

description: As AI lowers the barrier to creation, raw technical capability is no longer a differentiator. True success hinges on understanding customer taste as the secret sauce of business. Ultimately, the winners won't be the companies with the most AI, but those that stay closest to the humans they build for.

Financial independence isn’t just about money, it’s about having the freedom to choose how you spend your time. In this keynote, Rita Piçarra shares how she planned her path to financial independence and retired from corporate life at 44, after more than two decades in leadership roles. A practical and personal perspective on money, freedom, and taking ownership of the life you want to live.

title: The borderless advantage: How AI's fastest-growing companies are building world-class teams
description: The emerging cohort of AI decacorns is being built by founders who tap into the best talent, capital and opportunities across the world. As 87% of companies reaching US$100 million ARR in less than four years are launched by international founders, global talent has become the ultimate competitive edge. Drawing on his experience co-founding Prosper AI, Xavier de Gracia shares how frontier companies draw on international networks across the US and Europe to build elite teams and scale globally in the AI era.

title: The death of window shopping
description: When AI agents only buy what you request and social algorithms only echo past habits, where does that leave spontaneity? Cart.com co-founder Remington Tonar defends the digital storefront and cart—not as relic tools of the past, but as essential engines for emotional buying, unexpected discovery, and critical intent data in an automated world.

title: Does AI actually know what people want?
description: As AI makes it easier to build almost anything, how do we ensure we’re building the right things? As the barriers to creation fall, understanding human needs becomes more valuable than ever.

title: The physical shadow of the digital economy
description: AI agents can decide what to buy in milliseconds. But whatever they order still moves through a physical supply chain built over decades. Valentyn Frechka, inventor of a process that turns urban fallen leaves into paper packaging, argues that some of the biggest opportunities hide in the gaps between existing systems, and shares what it takes to turn one such connection into something that works at industrial scale.

title: AI needs ground to stand on
description: When an AI agent dispatches a delivery, triages an insurance claim, or prices the risk on a building in a flood plain, reasoning over text alone isn't enough. The decision has to be grounded in the physical world: where things are, how they're changing, and what's true right now. TomTom's Leo Sei shows what an agent needs to know about a place, at a time, before its decision survives contact with reality, as well as why one trusted location intelligence layer sits under logistics and insurance alike.

title: From local to limitless: Why creativity should know no boundaries

This talk explores how creative AI is helping brands overcome traditional barriers to growth, reimagining existing campaigns for new audiences without losing what makes them distinctive.

Beginning with high school students in France objecting to the declining conditions in their schools; these sentiments rapidly spread, across France and the rest of Europe, as people have taken to the streets to rebel against the increasing cost of living. We are joined by some of the leaders of these protests to discuss what drove them to take direct action, and why these protests are vital for the health of democracy.

title: AI wants your money. Can you trust it?

The future of AI isn't just about what agents can do. It's about what they're trusted to do.

title: The last mile for AI

A few are world builders.

title: Designed to disappear: Why developers and enterprises are building the next AI apps around Quiet Tech [Hosted by Even Realities]
description:
Most AI still lives in a chat window. But it could help most in a meeting, on a factory floor or on stage, where nobody can stop to look at a screen.

Even Realities G2 are everyday display smart glasses with no camera, built around Quiet Tech: they show you what you need, when you need it, then get out of the way. Hundreds of independent developers are already shipping apps for them.

In this masterclass, one of our top developers will share what makes a great app for a wearable display, why anyone who can build a web app can build for this ecosystem, and how companies are bringing ambient AI into everyday work—including a first look at what’s next for enterprise developers.

description: Every organisation has an agentic AI project, but identity and authentication often delay production-readiness. Using long-lived API keys, sharing credentials between humans and AI agents, and over-permissioning agents are anti-patterns that increase an organisation’s risk surface and prevent sustainable AI adoption.

Join fellow founders, innovators, and industry leaders pushing the boundaries of sustainable fashion to connect, exchange ideas, and shape what comes next. Build partnerships and drive meaningful change in one of the world's most impactful industries. See you there!

title: How physical AI is transforming the built environment
description: The AI conversation has been so focused on robots and self-driving cars, but there's a massive opportunity for AI that understands the physical spaces and buildings people already occupy. Learn from Verkada's Co-founder & CEO how advances in computer vision are transforming existing cameras into intelligent systems that improve security, safety, and operations across industries in real time, shifting organizations from reactive video review to proactive, AI-powered intervention.

title: UNICEF Tech for Good: Beyond the Hype
description: Forget the buzzwords. Discover how UNICEF puts AI, data and digital innovation to work for children around the world.   Meet our experts, explore solutions already at work and discover opportunities to create impact at scale.

title: Revolutionising retail
description: Explore the concepts and technologies that are transforming ecommerce and marketing, including innovations in digital advertising, content creation, customer engagement, and brand management. Delve into the future of retail, from the startups revolutionising shopping to the game-changing online marketplaces and supply-chain optimizations.

title: Beyond the pipeline: From single services to digital platforms
description: Selling commodity products or single transactional services is no longer enough. To thrive, companies must pivot into expansive digital platforms. Join us in exploring how established companies use their core infrastructure to launch high-margin digital products, AI-driven customer experiences and strategic partnerships, transforming traditional services into sticky, value-driven economies.

title: Break the browser monopoly
description: When big tech dictates how the internet works, developers lose autonomy and users lose privacy. This session explores the dangers of a consolidated browser market and the different ways independent players are fighting back through radical customisation, strict privacy protections and open web advocacy. See how a standards-forward approach is protecting essential privacy protocols. Together, these efforts ensure the open internet doesn't become a big tech-controlled walled garden.

title: East meets West: why AI products land differently across markets
description: The same AI product can be celebrated in one market and met with suspicion in another. Founders who built in China and are now scaling globally explain why that gap exists and how to build for both sides of it. How do users and investors in each market see AI? What do founders gain by combining China’s strengths with what Western audiences expect? And how do you earn trust across very different markets?

title: Zombie data: How your data comes back to haunt you
description: Is leaked data fueling hyper-personalised, AI-powered scams? Today’s cyber threats target trust rather than devices, using stolen profile data and session cookies to bypass passwords and MFA entirely. Traditional security asked if a file was dangerous, but modern security must ask if the moment itself is real.

title: Woke 3.0: The next generation of the culture wars?
description: From the social justice activism of Woke 1.0, through the backlash and recalibration of Woke 2.0, to Hasan Piker’s tongue-in-cheek declaration of Woke 3.0, progressive politics may be entering a new phase. But what has really changed? Is the left reclaiming its cultural confidence, shifting towards class and economic populism, or simply repackaging old battles for a new political moment? This talk explores the evolution of woke politics, the forces driving its reinvention and what Woke 3.0 might mean for the future of the American left.

Learn how the founders at the epicenter of this shift are empowering a new class of hyper-empowered talent to reshape media, entertainment, and digital culture

title: Build anything, anywhere
description: Ukraine has shown us that global disruptions burn through critical hardware faster than rigid assembly lines can replace it. Fragile overseas supply chains and multi-year factory tooling were built for a predictable world that no longer exists. Machina founder & CEO Edward Mehr breaks down the urgent shift toward decentralized production – revealing how networks of agile, software-defined factories deploy manufacturing directly to the point of need, securing industrial sovereignty across mobility, aerospace, and mission-critical supply chains.

title: What AI can do for humanity
description: In a tech landscape dominated by conversations about speed, efficiency, and scaling models, it’s easy to lose sight of why we build. Join Rodrigo Moran, Global Director of Creative at Microsoft as he cuts through the noise of AI hype to focus on what matters most: human-centric purpose. Discover how we can move beyond mere automation to design a future where AI truly serves humanity.

title: Open models, stronger ecosystems
description: Who gets to shape AI? Moonshot AI's answer is: everyone. Open models empower businesses and developers around the world to build, customise, and deploy AI around their own needs, supported by global inference providers. Following the launch of Kimi K3.1 Pro, Moonshot AI's most capable model to date, Director of International, Giacomo Ficari, shares the playbook for building ecosystems around open intelligence and taking frontier AI global.

title: Startup Matchbox: Open innovation for everyone
description: Startup Matchbox gives companies and startups of every size access to open innovation. Hear from some of the matches it made: how they found each other, what worked, and what’s next.

title: Selling sport: Has it gone too far?
description: Sport is becoming a global IP asset class. Multi-billion-dollar sports funds, private equity investments, media rights deals, and creator-driven franchises are reshaping how sport is valued, owned, and commercialised. But when FIFA tried to sell a stake in the World Cup this summer, the backlash showed there is a line. So, who actually owns the future value of sport?

title: Just raised $320 million. Now what?
description: Otter.ai just raised $320 million, more than six times what it raised in its first decade. With AI squeezing SaaS and meeting notetakers multiplying, the bet is enterprise: turning 40 million users into paying teams. In this session Sam Liang dives into what the money is for and how a SaaS company thrives in the age of AI.

title: Beyond walled gardens: Building the open web for AI agents
description: As AI agents take on more work, how will software and the internet need to change? Mazin Gilbert, executive director of the Agentic AI Foundation, and GoDaddy CEO Aman Bhutani explore what it takes for agents to work beyond proprietary platforms. From identity and permissions to tracing actions when things go wrong, Mazin and Aman discuss how open standards and industry collaboration can help developers build interoperable systems while keeping people in control.

description: AI has become a force multiplier for Intellectual Property abuse, therefore brands and other IP heavy businesses must adapt their operations and prepare their businesses for these challenges. Meet legal tech experts, lawyers and engineers to learn and swap notes at the intersection of law and technology.

title: Securing the AI frontline
description: Modern conflict no longer stays in the cloud. As state-sponsored actors and advanced cybercriminals target autonomous systems, critical infrastructure, and military hardware, the front line of cyber defense has been pushed to the limit. Now, it’s up to democratic nations to adapt, respond, and secure the tactical edge.

description: Discover how Open VSX and open source foundations help teams build AI products faster. Explore how startups such as Cursor and Windsurf use them to challenge established platforms and create new AI experiences at scale. Please be aware that attendance is first-come, first-served.

Please be aware that attendance is first-come, first-served.

Digital health founders: learn from a founder going through it how digital therapeutics get paid for, from Germany’s DiGA fast track to the NHS and insurers 💶 See you there!

title: CX in the Age of AI 👥
description:
As AI reshapes the future of work, leaders must bridge the gap between workforce design and customer experience. Join this meetup to discuss how leadership can earn trust in AI and empower teams to focus on delivering exceptional customer outcomes.

This session is limited to 100 people, with spots available on a first-come, first-served basis.

title: Small team, big screen - one person, one laptop, one award-winning film
description: A high-end short used to cost $500k. 'Website', winner of the Reply AI Film Festival, was made for $7k by the independent team behind DiDi_OK, with Jiaze leading the AI visuals from a single laptop. AI makes filmmaking more accessible, but great storytelling still requires human creativity and vision.

title: Western tech: All is not lost
description: Between aggressive state-backed tech models, supply chain rifts, and escalating geopolitical rivalries, headlines are quick to declare the decline of Western tech dominance. But is the game truly lost, or merely entering a more volatile, competitive chapter? Join leaders from Jasper, Legora, and Picsart as they examine the real state of play and what it will actually take to stay competitive on an increasingly divided global stage.

title: Inside the making of MOURINHO
description: Producer and Head of Development at Ventureland, Miles Coleman goes behind the scenes of MOURINHO, sharing how the documentary came together and exploring how the film captures one of football's most compelling figures and what its production reveals about the future of sports storytelling.

title: Innovation Pulse 2026: The Numbers Behind and the Road to 2027
description: How did Portugal’s innovation ecosystem perform in 2026? Join Unicorn Factory Lisboa as we reveal the key numbers behind this year’s growt, and share our vision and priorities for 2027.

title: Who wins when AI does the shopping?
description: For 25 years, retailers have competed to bring customers to their stores and influence what they buy. AI is beginning to change that equation. When an AI agent discovers, compares, and recommends, who controls the shopping decision? Maju Kuruvilla, Founder and CEO of Spangle AI and ex-Amazon VP, explores what retailers stand to lose, where new opportunities emerge, and how they can compete.

title: The World Cup effect: Portugal's global ambition
description: Portugal’s presence at the FIFA World Cup created an opportunity to showcase its football identity to a global audience. Nuno Gomes, Former Portugal international & High Performance Specialist at FIFA; João Medeiros Cardoso, Chief Marketing & Commercial Officer at the Portuguese Football Federation; discuss how commercial strategy, sponsorship and tourism can turn that visibility into lasting international growth and build a football powerhouse.

title: The future of politics: Swiping right on Gen-Z
description: Politicians love to say they want to "secure the youth vote", yet few are willing to step aside to make room for them. So, what does winning over this online generation actually take? Gen-Z is far from indifferent, they are redefining political power through digital activism and social justice. This panel of activists, strategists, creators, and journalists offers a candid look at the future of politics and how to campaign to a generation that doesn't just consume the conversation, but controls it.

title: Health's data shift: From episodic care to continuous prevention
description: Healthcare has long relied on sporadic snapshots like annual check-ups. Join Dor Kilroy, CCO at Oura, as she explores how continuous wearable data shifts medicine from reactive treatment to proactive prevention, and what it takes to scale those insights into better health outcomes.

title: Beyond the dashboard: how AI agents are rewiring finance operations
description: Finance teams still lose days reconciling payments, chasing invoices and updating systems by hand. Now, AI agents are moving beyond copilots and dashboards to take ownership of entire workflows. Caitlin, co-founder and CEO of Fazeshift, reveals why accounts receivable is becoming a proving ground for autonomous finance and what happens when software stops surfacing insights and starts owning outcomes.

title: AI watched 25 years of news. What did it see?
description: What happens when you process 25 years of global news across 100+ languages through modern AI? In this keynote, GDELT Project founder Kalev Leetaru unpacks the hidden geopolitical and cultural trends uncovered from millions of hours of global media and the software engineering required to build it. Step under the hood of planetary-scale data architecture to see how real-time NLP, automated translation and petabyte-scale pipelines can transform decades of chaotic global noise into clean, queryable data that developers can use to build new intelligent tools.

title: Pricing SaaS when users are agents
description: Per-seat pricing assumed a human was at the keyboard. As AI agents take over the work, the seat is a poor measure of value. LaunchDarkly charges for usage, not seats. Mindstone made his AI agent system free for up to 100 users, because the real value was in getting people to change how they work. They discuss what to charge for when the software itself is close to free.

title: Growth has rules: Speed breaks 'em
description: The growth playbook you're proud of might be the very thing slowing you down. Neha helped write the growth playbook at Twitter and Pinterest. Then she left to found JustAI and had to unlearn a lot of it. Starting from the ground up, Neha rethought what she knew, adapted and proved her assumptions wrong more than once. The rules survived, but the pace didn’t. What took weeks now takes hours. Trying is almost free and extremely fast, so the fastest teams set the records. In this talk, Neha shares what she unlearned, the rules that held up and how to keep those rules while breaking every record.

title: The real threat isn’t a nation-state, it’s a teenager.
description: Are you defending against headlines or reality? Most organizations spend millions defending against nation-state threats, while the attackers who actually get in fly under the radar. Join The Hacking Games CPO John Madelin and former child hacker Conor Freeman for a live ACE demo with the latest attack data captured from young hackers. Get inside the mind of an AI-equipped attacker to see where security is failing today and how to fix your real vulnerabilities.

From digital literacy and workforce development to inclusive innovation, the discussion asks how we can make AI work for the many and not the few.

title: Sound that belongs: How AI is changing music for video
description: What if the soundtrack was built around your video, not the other way around? Keli Li, co-founder of Sonilo and former head of global music at TikTok, and creator Joey Reed (6.2M followers on TikTok) discuss how AI is changing music for video: what creators actually need from audio, what usage rights a creator has from AI-generated music, and whether a perfect soundtrack is now one click away.

title: 📣 Beyond the stage for Latinas in tech with Cintia Mano
description: Join Cintia Mano, Good Latinas Chapter Leader for Iberia, in a beyond the stage meetup for Latinas in tech, business and investment. Far from home, but never alone: meet the Good Latinas for Good Iberia Chapter, discover how we can support and learn from each other, and leave with connections who really get you. 🤝🏽 See you there!

title: The human network: bingo, big ideas & beautiful connections
description:
Join the London School of Economics for a fast-paced, playful community experience that combines Human Bingo, systems thinking and entrepreneurial curiosity to explore how the most interesting ideas often emerge when unexpected people, perspectives and problems collide.

Limited capacity to 100 people, on a first-come, first-served basis.

description: Discover how Brazilian Bio & Health startups are developing innovative solutions that improve healthcare, well-being, and quality of life while addressing global challenges.

title: 🤳 Building a business on social meetup
description: Your best salesperson might be a 30-second video 🤳. Meet founders, marketers and social sellers turning content into customers, and swap notes on what's converting right now. See you there!

title: Just what the dev ordered: Healthcare’s AI revolution
description: Healthcare is notorious for its fragmented legacy software. Join Stellarus CTO Greg Ryslik as they discuss how today's engineers are rewriting the rules of clinical technology. Explore the modern data infrastructure behind a universal healthcare platform and see how developers can solve legacy healthcare problems.

title: Why physical AI needs a new architecture
description: Cloud infrastructure powered yesterday's digital services, but as AI moves into the physical world, centralised computing is hitting a wall. Real-time physical systems running transport and critical infrastructure cannot survive a round trip to a distant data centre. This session explores why, if you don’t control the infrastructure your AI runs on, you don’t truly control your AI.

title: Making silicon sexy: How Cerebras put hard tech in the spotlight
description: Technical breakthroughs aren’t enough to win Wall Street. You need a story that scales alongside your compute. This fireside conversation unpacks how to turn complex hardware innovation into a compelling narrative – one that captures attention, builds a category, and creates momentum on the road to a blockbuster IPO.

title: The smartphone in your pocket is your next lab
description: What if screening over 70 health biomarkers across 10+ organs took less than two minutes on a standard smartphone? YOU(th) founder & CEO Filippo Nigro reveals how machine learning and ubiquitous mobile sensors are democratising preventive longevity and transforming passive phones into active health screeners.

title: A̶I̶ Emotional Frontier
description: As marketing polarises between algorithmic noise and authentic human connection, the relentless attention economy is forcing brands to rethink how they communicate. Driven by audiences' demand for authenticity, Founder & CEO of Hey Honey, Chris Adams explores how emotion converts attention into community, customers, and superfans. In a world increasingly shaped by AI, making people feel is how brands win.

title: Building a brand from the baseline
description: Elite athletes are uniquely equipped to be founders -they process failure rapidly, execute under intense pressure and possess deep domain knowledge of what high-performance lifestyle and health products actually require. This panel dissects the operational realities, mental discipline and strategic advantage of building a startup from hotel rooms, locker rooms and international travel schedules.

timeslot_participations.name: Dylan Gee
timeslot_participations.job_title: Former pro tennis player and coach, creator of 'Tennis With Dylan'

title: Chinamaxxing: The new era of Made in China
description: From AI-powered glasses to self-balancing motorcycles, Chinese brands aren't just making gadgets anymore. They're reinventing them. The panel dives deep into what's behind China's tech glow-up, and why is the world suddenly paying attention?

title: Deus ex machina: Can AI replace God?
description: Religion and mythology have been used, for millenia, to seize power. As AI progresses in its capabilities, the narratives around it are taking on an increasingly religious, or theistic, tone. In this session we explore how these shifts in language are used by elites to obtain and entrench their power. Can AI replace God, and if it can, what does that mean for us?

title: eVTOL is taking off
description: Could your next commute be through the skys? Discover how electric vertical takeoff and landing aircraft compare to traditional helicopters and planes. This session explores where the technology is heading, its real-world applications, and what it takes to reshape daily travel.

title: There is no ghost in the machine
description: Code does not rebel – treating foundation models as autonomous entities turns ordinary software failures into acts of God, shielding companies from conventional product liability. Join Gabriele Mazzini as he explores how there is no sentient actor lurking in neural weights to fear or pacify; there are only engineers, product teams, and corporate boards deciding which guardrails are worth the latency cost and which shortcuts accelerate time to market.

timeslot_participations.name: Gabriele Mazzini
timeslot_participations.job_title: Architect of EU AI Act & Fellow

title: The perimeter is dead. So what happens to trust?
description: In an era of automated cyber warfare, is true digital resilience even possible? AI is accelerating targeted phishing, deepfake identity fraud, and data breaches. From corporate firewalls to global financial systems, traditional security perimeters are failing. This panel breaks down actionable self-defence strategies to empower enterprises, infrastructure leaders, and citizens to adapt, overcome, and thrive in an increasingly hostile cyber world.

title: Decoding planet Earth
description: Current AI models excel at predicting words, but understanding physical events in real time is a whole different challenge. The next AI frontier will be to teach machines how to perceive physical environments as they change. Developers will get a clear look at how systems ingest real-world signals, from live news and geodata to visual inputs, to better understand the world around us.

title: Betting against the moat
description: Every incumbent in enterprise software says the same thing: decades of proprietary data and workflow lock-in make them impossible to dislodge. Caitlin Leksana is betting that's exactly the kind of confidence that goes extinct once AI agents can do the job end to end – and Rocio Wu backed her with millions of investor dollars to prove it. In this session, Caitlin and Rocio debate whether a 'moat' still means anything in enterprise software, or whether it's just what the losing side says on the way out.

title: AI sprawl is exploding. Get ahead of governance and security challenges before it’s boo late
description: The rapid surge of AI and autonomous agents introduces risks that traditional security measures cannot address, placing new demands on organisations to govern AI sprawl across the enterprise. Learn how top organisations gain visibility over their AI infrastructure through practical strategies for discovering AI assets, implementing governance frameworks, orchestrating agent workflows and maintaining accountability in AI-driven decisions.

title: 🎬 Entertainment & media leaders meetup
description: Join fellow media executives, entertainment founders and content leaders for a meetup! Come connect with people shaping the future of content, streaming and storytelling. See you there!

title: 🥷 Solo founders meetup
description: Building a startup on your own? You don't have to network alone 🥷! Meet fellow solo founders, swap notes on doing it all and find people who get it. See you there!

title: 📲 Mobile developers meetup
description: Building for the screen in everyone’s pocket? Meet iOS, Android and cross-platform developers, and swap notes on performance, app store wins and what users really tap on 📲 See you there!

title: Reset velocity: from attention to connection
description: Social media is undergoing a fundamental reset. After years of rewarding visibility, performance and reach, people are moving towards more private, authentic and participatory spaces where meaningful connections matter most. Ronan Harris and Lea Karam will explore how this shift is taking shape across markets and what it means for the future of brands and advertising. They'll unpack why connection is becoming a more powerful currency than attention, and how brands can stay relevant in a world where influence increasingly happens beyond the public feed.

title: Three companies before product-market fit: What each one taught us
description: Building a high-growth company rarely happens on the first try. Bruno, founder of Cumbuca, breaks down the hard-won lessons from his previous startups. From building products nobody needed to battling unit economics, and how applying those failures turned Cumbuca B2B into a profitable platform powering data consent for over 10 million users through open finance.

title: Portugal's new wave of influence
description: The lines between entertainment, personal branding and entrepreneurship are increasingly blurred. As actors, artists and digital creators build audiences beyond traditional media, new opportunities are emerging to turn influence into businesses, partnerships and brands. Júlia Palha and Bárbara Corby discuss how Portugal's next generation of talent is navigating this changing landscape and building careers in the digital economy.

timeslot_participations.job_title: Journalist & Presenter, The Next Big Idea

title: StartUP VISA | Global Talent to Business Success
description: IAPMEI, a StartUP Visa entrepreneur and a certified incubator discuss how they can work together to build and grow a promising innovative project in Portugal and attract diverse international talent.

title: Search built for AI agents
description: AI agents are on track to search the web more than humans, and their answers are only as good as the data they find. This session breaks down the infrastructure of agentic search and how it directly determines AI accuracy, speed, and cost.

title: Hollywood's identity crisis
description: Deepfakes and generative AI are creating new threats to Hollywood, putting the likeness, voice and creative rights of artists at risk. As the technology races ahead, who gets to decide how an artist’s identity is used? Dan Neely and Duncan Crabtree-Ireland explore how the industry can protect performers from exploitation while using the same technology to safeguard their rights and put control back in their hands.

title: Spatial intelligence in physical retail
description: While e-commerce captures every click, scroll, and drop-off, physical stores still generate most retail sales in the dark. This session reveals how turning inventory into a real-time data signal maps the shopper journey, uncovers high-performing store zones, and shows exactly where intent becomes a sale.

title: Achieving the impossible
description: Professional big-wave surfer Lucas “Chumbo” Chianca and skimboarding world champion Lucas Fink are pushing the limits of what athletes can achieve, sharing perspectives on taking on Nazaré’s monster waves and connecting with global audiences. This session draws inspiration from the risks, mindset and determination behind their sport, exploring how extraordinary performances can translate into global recognition, major sponsorships and new opportunities for athletes and brands.

timeslot_participations.name: Ben Jacobs
timeslot_participations.job_title: Premier League Reporter & Senior Football Correspondent

title: Integration or assimilation? The immigration debate
description: Immigration is reshaping European politics, with parties once on the margins now winning significant support amid public concern over housing, security and national identity. Governments have responded with measures ranging from tighter border controls to reduced work permits. Our panel asks: what do we expect of newcomers once they arrive? Should they adopt the host society’s culture and norms through assimilation, or should societies make room for cultural difference within a shared civic framework via integration?

title: Rebuilding open source with AI: Lessons Learned
description: How we write software has fundamentally changed. Where we used to sweat over every little detail in source files, we now spend most of our time discussing high level direction with our agents. Prisma CEO Søren Bramer Schmidt shares lessons learned from rewriting Prisma from scratch with AI. Learn how to make the most of coding agents in 2026, and how the changing landscape affects open source libraries.

title: MIT €100K: designed in Portugal, built for the world
description: The MIT €100K introduces a national entrepreneurship competition empowering innovative projects from Portuguese universities through mentoring, training and access to global innovation networks. The winning team earns the chance to pitch at MIT in Boston. The session will showcase the competition’s second edition, selection process and opportunities, featuring insights from first-edition winner RTBeamTech.

title: Critical minerals in the next AI frontier
description: AI has fundamentally transformed the digital world, but that same transformation in the physical world is just beginning. Using mineral exploration as an example, Terra AI co-founder and CEO John Mern shows how combining domain science with frontier AI can unlock breakthroughs that traditional scaling can't reach. He highlights how these innovations are disrupting one of the oldest and most foundational heavy industries in the world, and identifies other underserved fields ready for similar disruption. For innovators and investors, the challenge made is to bet on humanity by building AI for the most critical physical-world problems.

title: Beyond the front door: Identity, access, and user trust
description: AI deepfakes don’t stop at the front door, they target every stage of the user lifecycle from initial onboarding to internal access. But stronger security shouldn't come at the cost of privacy. This session will explore how identity verification and privileged access management converge to prevent fraud and protect privacy.

title: Digital transformation and dynamism in service delivery
description: How can governments and international organisations use digital technology to make public services faster, simpler and more accessible? This talk discusses how modernisation is increasingly taking the form of AI, digital identity and online services, along with the challenges around security, inclusion and implementation at scale.

title: What if every B2B buyer had a store built just for them?
description: B2B buyers want the same easy experience they get as consumers, with their own catalogs, negotiated prices, payment terms and approval flows. A Solution Engineer will demo how VTEX personalizes the B2B journey for each company and buyer, so they can order on their own at scale.

title: 📚 Edtech startups meetup
description: What's the next big shift in Edtech? Debate it with peers who are living it 🚀. Connect with peers shaping the future of your field. Looking forward to seeing you!

title: Who gets a say in football’s future?
description: Football belongs to billions, yet the people who play, watch and love the game rarely have a say in how it evolves. World Cup winner and Common Goal co-founder Juan Mata joins Jürgen Griesbeck, co-founder of Common Goal and C-Lab, to introduce Unleash Football, an initiative designed to give football's global community a greater voice in shaping the game's future. They'll share early insights from voices around the world, what people want from football and what they believe needs to change, before inviting the audience to add their voice live.

title: Zero turbulence: The AI engine behind global travel
description: When a global platform processes round-the-clock transactions, downtime isn't an option. In this session, Michael Esquibel explores how AI and intelligent automation help maintain always-on servicing for companies. In a world of surging demand and increased disruption, discover how AI-driven processes can prevent service interruption and get travellers where they need to be.

title: Investigative journalism under threat
description: Investigative journalism faces mounting threats across the UK and Europe, including restrictive libel laws, misuse of privacy claims, SLAPPs, intimidation and reputational attacks. This panel will examine efforts to silence critical reporting, the protection available to journalists, and how online safety laws, platform moderation and algorithms may affect independent media.

title: EIT Jumpstarter Awards Ceremony
description:
Join us to celebrate the winners of EIT Jumpstarter 2026! Discover Europe's most promising early-stage innovators and their groundbreaking solutions, followed by a networking cocktail reception.

Register here - https://luma.com/a2ue9hpo


EIT Jumpstarter is a pre-acceleration programme of the European Institute of Innovation and Technology (EIT), a body of the European Union. It helps early-stage innovators turn science-based ideas into startups through training, mentoring and an international pitch competition. The programme is delivered by EIT Urban Mobility, EIT Food, EIT Health, EIT RawMaterials and InnoEnergy, together with Xjenza Malta.
